questions.:question/problem:
Find the exact value of $$
\displaystyle {\cos }^{2}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{12}\right)-{\sin }^{2}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{12}\right).
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{\cos }^{2}⁡x-{\sin }^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\cos }^{2}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{12}\right)-{\sin }^{2}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{12}\right) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{12}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

questions.:question/worked-solution:
Use the cosine double-angle identity:

$$
\cos^2\left(x\right)-\sin^2\left(x\right)=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute the angle and evaluate the standard-angle cosine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\cos^2\left(\frac{7\pi}{8}\right)-\sin^2\left(\frac{7\pi}{8}\right) \\
&= \cos\left(2\cdot \frac{7\pi}{8}\right) \\
&= \cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{4}\right) \\
&= \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \\
&= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$
